fields.meta_title: 5K Registration Form Builder for Race Directors | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a 5K registration form that works out age groups on race day and numbers every bib in registration order. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a 5K Registration Form With Age Groups and Bibs
fields.hero_description: Build a 5K registration form that places runners in age groups by race day and saves every entry to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Race Morning Needs From Every Entry
fields.features_subheading: A sheet of names still leaves someone sorting age groups and shirt sizes by hand. These six pieces sort them as runners register.
fields.feature_1:
Age groups set by the race date

Runners enter a birth date, and the app works out their age on race day, not on the day they register. Each runner lands in a 5-year band, such as Women 40-44, for the results.
fields.feature_2:
The 5K and the kids' mile on one form

Offer a 5K run, a 5K walk, and a 1-mile kids' dash on the same form. Each distance asks only its own questions, so walkers skip the expected finish time that runners give.
fields.feature_3:
Waivers signed before the entry saves

Show the race waiver as a required step and capture the runner's signature. When the birth date puts a runner under 18, a guardian section opens and asks a parent to sign too.
fields.feature_4:
Shirt sizes counted for the printer

Every entry adds to a running count of S, M, L, and XL. On the shirt order date, the race director gets the totals by email, and any later entry is flagged for leftover stock.
fields.feature_5:
Bib numbers in registration order

Each runner gets the next bib number the moment the entry saves, starting from any number you pick. At packet pickup, volunteers search by last name and mark each packet collected.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the race site where your club already runs things. Every runner record sits in a database you own.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Races and What Each One Needs
fields.tab_content_1:
23 runners on Night Shift Nurses, each emailed to Marisol

Fernbrook Hospice runs its 5K with 31 teams, and every runner picks one from a list on the form or starts a new one. Night Shift Nurses now has 23 runners. Team captain Marisol Quintero gets an email each time someone joins, with the runner's name and the team's new count.
fields.tab_content_2:
Guardians sign for any runner under 18

Birth dates decide who signs at the Alder Creek Elementary fun run on April 18. A parent enters a birth date of June 2, 2016. The app works out that the runner will be 9 on race day, and a guardian section opens below the waiver. Tomasz Wierzbicki signs for his daughter Hana, and only then does the entry save.
fields.tab_content_3:
All 842 shirt sizes counted before the order goes in

Shirts for the Quarry Lake Turkey Trot go to the printer on November 3. That morning, race director Ottoline Barrasford gets an email with the count from 842 entries: 168 S, 291 M, 236 L, and 147 XL. Anyone who registers after the order goes in is flagged for leftover stock.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bib 417 goes out after one last-name search

Packet pickup opens at 6:30 a.m. at the Kestrel Valley Harvest 5K. A volunteer types Okonkwo on the tablet and finds Adaeze Okonkwo with bib 417 in Women 40-44. Her shirt is a size M. One tap marks her packet picked up, and the count reads 388 of 520 packets.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a 5K Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a 5K registration form that sorts runners by age group and has every bib ready for packet pickup.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what race day uses
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the waiver in the flow
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the race date, the start time, each distance, and the field limit before you open the form builder. The race date matters most, because every runner's age group is worked out from that one day.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick the bands your results will use, such as 5-year groups from 14 and under up to 70 and over, split by gender. Count each runner's age on race day. A runner whose birthday falls that week then lands in the right group.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Keep the questions to what someone will act on: name, birth date, gender, email, an emergency contact, and shirt size. Add an expected finish time only if you seed runners into corrals at the start line.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste in the waiver text your race uses and make the signature a required step. Add a guardian section for runners under 18 that a parent signs before the entry saves, and keep each signed waiver on the runner's record.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the distances and age groups into one prompt, along with the waiver text and the shirt order date. Emergent builds the form with a database of runners behind it and a pickup screen for volunteers. Change any question later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set the shirt and bib rules
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the date the shirt order goes to the printer and who gets the size totals that morning. Then choose the first bib number, and decide whether walkers get a range of their own that starts at 1000.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter a test runner born 12 years before race day and check that the guardian section opens. Then search that last name on the pickup screen and confirm the bib number and age group match what the test entry says.

faq_plan.a: A 5K registration form is how runners enter a 5K, a road race of 5 kilometers, or about 3.1 miles. It collects who each runner is and how to reach them, along with a signed waiver. The race director uses those entries to set age groups and assign bibs.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a 5K registration form?
faq_plan.a: Decide the distances and age groups, then describe them in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, along with the waiver. Emergent builds the form and the database of runners behind it. Share the link once one made-up runner has gone through from start to finish.

faq_plan.q: What should a 5K registration form template include?
faq_plan.a: A 5K registration form template needs each runner's name, birth date, gender, email, and phone, plus an emergency contact. Add the distance and a shirt size, then the waiver signature. Leave out a mailing address unless you mail packets ahead of race day, because nobody reads it on race morning.

faq_plan.q: Why does a 5K registration form ask for a birth date?
faq_plan.a: Set age groups by how old each runner will be on race day, and a birth date is the one answer that stays correct. A runner who types an age in March may be a year older by the race in June. A general registration form can skip the question, but a race with age-group awards cannot.

faq_plan.q: How do you assign bib numbers from a 5K registration form?
faq_plan.a: Assign them in the order runners register, starting from a number you choose, such as 101. Give walkers or the kids' dash their own range if the timing crew needs to tell them apart. The app gives each runner a bib when the entry saves, and the pickup list is ready before race week.

faq_plan.q: Should a 5K registration form include a waiver?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put it on the form as a required step, not on a separate sheet at the start line. A waiver signed during registration stays attached to that runner's entry and cannot be skipped. Use the wording your race already relies on. An app built with Emergent captures each signature with the entry.

faq_plan.q: Can one 5K registration form cover a 5K and a kids' dash?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Offer each distance as the first choice, then show only the questions that distance needs. The kids' dash asks for a youth shirt size, while the 5K asks for an expected finish time. It works like the session picks on a conference registration form: one entry, with a different path for each choice.

faq_plan.q: Can a 5K registration form take race-day entries?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set up a tablet at a walk-up table that opens the same form runners used online. Each walk-up entry gets the next bib on the same list, and the shirt count updates with it. Close walk-ups 30 minutes before the start to give volunteers time with the last bibs. An app built with Emergent keeps every entry in a database you own, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: When should a 5K registration form close?
faq_plan.a: Close it 2 days before the race, once the bib list goes to the printer and the pickup list is final. Runners who miss the cutoff can still enter at the walk-up table. Print the closing date at the top of your 5K registration forms and on the race page.

faq_plan.q: What should a 5K registration form ask about kids who run?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the child's birth date, a youth shirt size, and a guardian's name and phone number. A race only needs to know who the child is and who to call. A daycare registration form asks far more, such as who may pick the child up, and none of that belongs on a race entry.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Cognito Forms, Jotform, Typeform, Formstack) and race-director guides that list the same fields: name, email, address, gender, shirt size. None of them shows what a race director does with those fields. This page treats the 5K registration form as the start of race operations: an age group worked out from the birth date on race day, a guardian signature that appears only for minors, shirt totals ready for the printer's deadline, team rosters for charity runs, and a bib list a volunteer can search at packet pickup, with every runner saved as a row in a database the organizer owns.
